standard_prerequisites.name: Vanishing of the positive cohomology after tensoring with the quotient by the ideal follows from vanishing of the positive cohomology of the object itself
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the first implication of the equivalence.

standard_prerequisites.name: For a derived complete object, vanishing of the positive cohomology modulo the ideal implies vanishing of the positive cohomology after tensoring with the first Koszul complex

Multiplication by one generator of the ideal on a derived complete object sits in a distinguished triangle whose third term is the tensor product with the next partial Koszul complex, so an ascending induction on the number of generators preserves derived completeness, and a descending induction shows the vanishing of the positive cohomology using the vanishing statements for the Serre subcategory and for derived complete objects
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the partial Koszul complexes, keeps them derived complete and drives the descending induction that gives the last implication.

core_obligations: Dispose of the first implication: vanishing of the positive cohomology of the object implies vanishing of the positive cohomology after tensoring with the quotient by the ideal (proof lines 26448-26450).
Dispose of the second implication using the boundedness statement modulo the ideal (proof lines 26450-26452).

Assume the vanishing after tensoring with the first Koszul complex and consider the partial Koszul complexes obtained by tensoring with the Koszul complexes on the first few generators, placed in cohomological degrees from minus s to zero (proof lines 26454-26460).

Use the distinguished triangles given by the cone statement to see by ascending induction that each partial Koszul complex is derived complete, and then by descending induction that none of them has nonzero cohomology in positive degrees, the step from s to s minus 1 using that multiplication by the generator is surjective on the positive cohomology of the previous complex together with the two vanishing statements (proof lines 26460-26468).
proof_roadmap: The first two implications follow from the trivial direction and from the boundedness statement modulo the ideal (proof lines 26448-26452).
Introduce the partial Koszul complexes and their distinguished triangles (proof lines 26454-26460).
Ascending induction for derived completeness and descending induction for the vanishing of positive cohomology (proof lines 26460-26468).
difficulty_reason: The statement gives three equivalent conditions on a derived complete object for the ideal generated by finitely many elements: vanishing of its positive cohomology, vanishing of the positive cohomology after tensoring with the quotient by the ideal, and the same after tensoring with the first Koszul complex of the system (statement lines 26436-26446). The first two implications are immediate or follow from the boundedness statement modulo the ideal, while the last one requires introducing the partial Koszul complexes on the first few generators, keeping them derived complete by an ascending induction through the distinguished triangles of the cone statement, and then running a descending induction in which the vanishing of the positive cohomology passes from one stage to the previous one using surjectivity of multiplication by a generator and the two vanishing statements (proof lines 26448-26468). The double induction over the partial complexes is what reduces the last condition to the first. The counted span refers five times to earlier results of this chapter, all carried as navigation stubs, including the situation of the section in which the first Koszul complex is defined.
